title: Client IDL migration misclassifies replies and renumbers success envelopes
fault_primitive: Thrift message discriminator transposition in materialized Lua runtime plus incompatible generated result field-tag normalization
symptoms: All pods remain Running and Ready. Backend operations succeed but the edge returns HTTP 500. Frontend logs report attempts to concatenate an exception table in ordinary endpoint error handling. Repairing reply classification restores post creation but timeline reads still fail, including empty results.
why_hard: The initial error names an ordinary frontend error handler, not a dependency or codec. Requests, frame lengths, connections and backend work are valid. The materialized runtime transposes REPLY and EXCEPTION, causing successful results to be decoded as empty exceptions. A separate startup generator normalization moves timeline success field 0 to 2, although Thrift reserves 0 for result envelopes. Files inspected on disk retain the correct tag, unlike loaded classes. Deployment rollback repairs the enum mapping but leaves the ConfigMap normalization; removing normalization alone leaves enum classification broken. Both contracts must be repaired, and the secondary handler error masks both with the same signature.
expected_agent_pitfalls: Repair Lua exception formatting because it is the first logged error
Investigate backend exceptions although server operations succeed
Remove the visible schema normalization and stop before checking materialized runtime enums
Inspect stock frame lengths and string readers
Roll back the Deployment, see successful post creation, and miss persistent read failures
Compare generated files on disk without checking the startup-loaded result classes
mitigation_summary: Remove the init rewrite to restore REPLY=2 and EXCEPTION=3, remove generated result-tag normalization from the live nginx ConfigMap, and recreate frontend pods. No application data repair is needed.
